Emergency general surgery laparotomies are indeed an area of concern, with a high rate of mortality, particularly in patients over 70 years old. To improve outcomes, several strategies can be employed, such as increasing acute surgical care manpower, early recognition of patients requiring emergency surgery, developing clear management protocols, and considering centralization of emergency surgical services to specialist centers with multidisciplinary teams. This would involve collaboration between emergency surgeons and care of the elderly physicians, both in hospital and in related community outreach services for post-discharge care. 

It's worth noting that measuring hospital mortality rates, even up to 180 days post-admission, may not yield a significantly different perspective than using 30-day data. However, the primary focus should be on improving care and reducing mortality rates, especially in high-risk groups. By addressing these concerns and implementing targeted improvements, it may be possible to reduce mortality rates and enhance overall patient outcomes in emergency general surgery laparotomies.
